column2: Risti by Sigbjørn Obstfelder is a novella written in the late 19th century. This lyrical, introspective love story follows a first-person narrator and the mercurial Rebekka as their consuming affair awakens rapture, jealousy, and spiritual longing, with the sculptor Bredo emerging as a troubling presence.

A third day in Mary Carrow's school by Anonymous is a didactic children’s Sunday-school tale written in the mid-19th century. It presents a gentle picture of rural schooling and moral formation, likely aimed at young readers and their families, focusing on everyday lessons, play, nature study, and simple Christian teaching.

Ameno Kamato by André Lebey is a mythological prose-poem written in the early 20th century. Rooted in Shinto lore, it transforms a cosmic crisis into an allegory of war, devastation, and renewal, where ritual, dance, and music restore the harmony of nature and the light of the sun.
Dressed vegetables à la mode by Mrs. De Salis is a cookbook written in the late 19th century.

My Past and Thoughts (Russian: Былое и думы, romanized: Byloje i dumy) is an extensive autobiography by Alexander Herzen, which he started in the early 1850s and continued to expand and revise throughout his later life. Serialized in Polyarnaya Zvezda, the book in its full form came out as a separate edition after its author's death.
Opa en Ineke by A. Hubert van Beusekom is a collection of children's stories written in the early 20th century.

Lord Lister No. 0042: Ongewenschte wraak by Kurt Matull and Theo von Blankensee is a serialized crime novella written in the early 20th century. It follows the gentleman-thief Lord Lister (Raffles) and his aide Charly Brand as they take on a brazen crime committed in Raffles’s name and the apparent ruin of a prominent shipowner.

Bound south by Ernest Haycox is a Western short story written in the early to mid-20th century. It centers on a drifting cowboy’s run-in with a lawless cowtown and the tests of loyalty and nerve that follow.
Sixteen to One on Friday by W. C.

Stories of gypsy life by Konrad Bercovici is a collection of short stories written in the early 20th century. It evokes Romani and Romanian village life in and around the Carpathians, exploring work, love, honor, and the pull between ancestral customs and encroaching modern ways.

Partners in Crime is a short story collection by British writer Agatha Christie, first published by Dodd, Mead and Company in the US in 1929 and in the UK by William Collins, Sons on 16 September of the same year. The US edition retailed at $2.00 and the UK edition at seven shillings and sixpence (7/6).

A simplified presentation of Einstein's unified field equations by Levi-Civita is a technical guide written in the early 21st century. The text likely focuses on preparing math-heavy HTML sources for publication, converting MathJax expressions to SVG images, and managing workflows for updates and corrections.

Gyurkovicsin pojat by Ferenc Herczeg is a novel written in the late 19th century. It is a witty, satirical family chronicle set in the Austro‑Hungarian world, following the exuberant Gyurkovics clan—especially the hot‑blooded twin Géza and his gentler brother András—through scrapes with schoolmasters, the army, society, and first love.
Le major A. Gordon Laing (Tombouctou 1826) by A.

La captive des Mohawks by Edward Sylvester Ellis is a frontier adventure novel written in the mid-19th century. Set on the post-Revolutionary New York frontier, it centers on settler Alfred Haverland, his spirited daughter Ina, and the shrewd Yankee scout Seth Jones as they confront Mohawk raiders; the plot quickly becomes a high-stakes captivity-and-rescue tale that also draws in the determined young hunter Everar

Meren äärillä by Larin-Kyösti is a collection of poetry written in the early 20th century. The book evokes seafaring and island life in the northern Baltic, blending nature lyricism with village portraits; its likely topic is the sea’s power and the daily rhythms, dangers, and celebrations of coastal communities.

Bonny bairns by Amy Ella Blanchard is an illustrated collection of children’s poems and nursery verses from the late 19th century. It gently celebrates everyday childhood, blending family warmth, play, manners, and nature into soothing, affectionate pieces meant for reading aloud.

Abenteurer by Knut Hamsun is a collection of short stories written in the early 20th century. It follows drifting laborers and outsiders in America, charting harsh prairie work, rail-side wandering, and fraught moral choices.

Plainte contre inconnu by Pierre Drieu La Rochelle is a novel written in the early 20th century. It sketches a postwar portrait of disillusioned young men in Paris, especially a veteran, Guy La Marche, seen through a sharp, introspective narrator amid bars, theaters, and drifting salons.

Sitka, the snow baby by Allen Chaffee is a children’s nature-adventure story written in the early 20th century. It likely blends fiction and natural history, following a polar bear cub named Sitka through Alaska’s seas, shores, and mountains while observing wildlife, weather, and Indigenous life, and then shifts to a second tale about a seal pup and a fisherman’s son.

The early worm by Robert Benchley is a collection of humorous essays written in the early 20th century. With droll, deadpan wit, it skewers modern habits, public fads, urban inconveniences, and historical myths through parodies, mock interviews, absurd reports, and running comic conceits.

Naamioita I-II by Eino Leino is a collection of verse dramas and playlets written in the early 20th century. The work blends Finnish myth and lyrical allegory to explore love, temptation, power, and conscience, following figures such as Väinämöinen and Aino, and the wanderer Äidin Kuopus with his devoted Kultahelkka as they face fateful choices.

De goudzoekers by Gustave Aimard is a novel written in the mid-19th century. It follows the buccaneer Montbars the Exterminator, his fierce follower Tributor, and comrades as they slip into Spanish-held waters near the Gulf of Venezuela to reconnoiter and prepare a daring strike on Maracaibo.

Ames d'Occident by Anatole Le Braz is a collection of short stories written in the late 19th century. Set in rural Brittany, it portrays village life, belief, and custom with a blend of humor, tenderness, and folkloric intensity.
The Andaman Islanders by A. R.
Lord Lister No. 0044: Het briljanten halssnoer van Flora Palmerston by Kurt Matull et al. is a pulp crime novella written in the early 20th century. It centers on gentleman-thief John C.

Lääkärin tunnustus by Milka Pogačić is a novel written in the early 20th century. Through a doctor's intimate confession to his son, it probes how a once-idyllic marriage is corroded by jealousy, secrecy, and moral doubt.

Gyurka ja Sándor by Ferenc Herczeg is a comic novel written in the early 20th century. It follows the high-spirited Gyurkovics brothers, Gyurka and Sándor, whose pranks, bravado, and run-ins with teachers, soldiers, and small-town society drive a lively coming-of-age tale.

My Past and Thoughts (Russian: Былое и думы, romanized: Byloje i dumy) is an extensive autobiography by Alexander Herzen, which he started in the early 1850s and continued to expand and revise throughout his later life. Serialized in Polyarnaya Zvezda, the book in its full form came out as a separate edition after its author's death.

Serialized in Polyarnaya Zvezda, the book in its full form came out as a separate edition after its author's death.

Martin Birck's youth by Hjalmar Söderberg is a novel written in the early 20th century. It follows the sensitive, observant Martin Birck from childhood into young adulthood in Stockholm, charting his family affections, first friendships and desires, and the growth of a skeptical, self-questioning mind amid a rapidly modernizing city.

The gold standard by Horace White is an economic essay and historical sketch written in the late 19th century. It examines monetary systems and policy, arguing for the single gold standard over bimetallism.

Only a girl-wife by Ruth Lamb is a domestic novel written in the late 19th century. It traces the adoption, rise, and romance of Andrew Crawford—a gifted young doctor raised by the kindly country physician Dr.
Taiteilijan lemmentarina by V. M.

Vindspel by Sigrid Backman is a novel written in the early 20th century. This lyrical, nature-steeped tale follows the sensitive young Astri as she spends a summer with her mentor Helma at a secluded lakeside home, where solitude, art, and a visiting painter named Sven awaken feelings she struggles to name.

The nature of living matter by Lancelot Thomas Hogben is a collection of scientific essays on biology and philosophy written in the early 20th century. The work probes what “life” means in scientific terms, weighing mechanistic against vitalistic views, and argues that biology’s methods align with those of physics, treating mind as behaviour and keeping science ethically neutral.

Le livre des singularités by Gabriel Peignot is an erudite miscellany of curiosities written in the early 19th century. It gathers playful yet learned notes, extracts, and anecdotes across theology, philology, history, literature, and everyday oddities into a cabinet of wonders.
Germantown old and new by Edwin C. Jellett is a historical and horticultural account written in the early 20th century.

The knitting teacher's assistant by Elvina Mary Corbould is an instructional manual written in the Victorian era, likely in the late 19th century. Aimed at teachers and pupils in girls’ schools, it provides practical, step-by-step guidance on knitting, with a clear focus on making stockings and socks to standard sizes.

The Crime Code by William Le Queux is a crime-thriller novel written in the early 20th century. It likely follows Lionel Hipwell, a rising Foreign Office man and would‑be MP, who becomes a fugitive after a fatal street struggle and is swept into a labyrinth of jewel thieves, espionage, and high-stakes intrigue that stretches from London’s underworld to Continental diplomatic salons.
Photography at home by John A. Tennant is a practical instructional handbook written in the early 20th century.

“Little Merry Christmas” by Winifred Arnold is a holiday novella written in the early 20th century. The tale centers on Mary “Merry Christmas” Christie, a spirited thirteen-year-old missionary’s daughter who arrives as a surprise at her gruff great-uncle Lemuel Perkins’s home in snowy Oatka Centre and, through cheer, courage, and kitchen magic, warms his heart and unites the village around the true spirit of the seas

Ilojen kaupunki by Arnold Bennett is a novel written in the early 20th century. It centers on the dazzling launch of a colossal London amusement park, where visionary conductor-impresario Charles Carpentaria and his moneyed partner Josephus Ilam clash over art, business, and control.
Knots by Arthur F. Aldridge is an instructional manual on marlinespike seamanship written in the early 20th century.

My Past and Thoughts (Russian: Былое и думы, romanized: Byloje i dumy) is an extensive autobiography by Alexander Herzen, which he started in the early 1850s and continued to expand and revise throughout his later life. Serialized in Polyarnaya Zvezda, the book in its full form came out as a separate edition after its author's death.

Lord Lister No. 0045: Het gestolen dienstmeisje by Matull and Blankensee is a pulp crime-adventure serial written in the early 20th century. The tale follows gentleman–master thief John Raffles (Lord Lister) and his aide Charly Brand as they mete out flamboyant, vigilante-style justice in London while running rings around Inspector Baxter.

Réflexions sur Stendhal by René Boylesve is a collection of literary reflections and reading notes written in the early 20th century. It is a work of literary criticism that sketches a thoughtful, unsystematic portrait of Stendhal as a psychologist of passion and a fiercely independent observer, considering how his inner vision resists social conventions; the likely topic is Stendhal’s temperament, aesthetics, and th

Anarchism is not enough by Laura Riding is a collection of critical essays written in the early 20th century. It examines social myth, language, and the arts to argue for a radically anti-social conception of poetry that refuses systems, utility, and cultural consolations.
An odd couple by Mrs. Oliphant is a novel written in the late 19th century.

A doorway in Fairyland by Laurence Housman is a collection of fairy tales written in the late 19th to early 20th century. These ornate, dreamlike tales follow humble lovers, guileless wanderers, and steadfast children as they bargain with moon-fays, wish through enchanted vessels, ride impossible tools, and test their courage for love.

Empfindungen aus meinem Leben by Amand Berghofer is a collection of lyrical and philosophical reflections—interweaving poems and prose meditations—written in the late 18th century. In the sentimental, nature-centered vein, it explores the inner life of a reflective narrator who turns from urban vanity to the healing presence of nature, the claims of love and virtue, and the consolations of faith, with a persistent at

A geographical and commercial view of northern Central Africa by James MacQueen is a geographical and economic treatise written in the early 19th century. It argues that the Niger and major eastern tributaries unite and empty into the Atlantic through the Bights of Benin and Biafra, and frames this claim within a plan for British-led inland commerce and gradual reform of slavery.

Salon soittaja by Larin-Kyösti is a collection of narrative poems and ballads written in the early 20th century. Drawing on Finnish folklore, nature mysticism, and village life, the book evokes myths, legends, and moral tales set amid forests, rapids, bogs, and fells.

The platypus by Harry Burrell is a natural history monograph written in the early 20th century. It presents a comprehensive, field-based account of the animal’s discovery, classification debates, anatomy, senses, habits, reproduction, nesting, range, captivity, and conservation, supported by photographs and plates.

Mimózák és krizántémok by Ignácz Kúnos is a collection of folktales written in the early 20th century. It presents Japanese fairy tales and legends in musical, rhyme-rich retellings, framed by a reflective essay on Japan’s spirit, nature-worship, and the Shinto-Buddhist outlook.

A Secret Agent in Port Arthur by Wirt Gerrare is a first-person war memoir and journalistic account written in the early 20th century. It follows an incognito newspaper operative moving through Russia and Manchuria—above all the besieged fortress of Port Arthur—during the Russo-Japanese War, mixing eyewitness reporting with reflections on espionage, censorship, and military life.

Moloch by Beulah Marie Dix is a play written in the early 20th century. It is a wartime domestic drama that charts how a comfortable household is consumed by the machinery of modern conflict, invoking the figure of Moloch as a metaphor for war’s demand for the young and the best.

Landesverein Sächsischer Heimatschutz — Mitteilungen Band XVI, Heft 9–12 is a regional heritage journal issue written in the early 20th century. This special compilation examines the catastrophic flood in the eastern Ore Mountains, pairing scientific analysis with historical context and practical proposals.

Maininki ja vaahtopää by Aaro Hellaakoski is a collection of poems written in the early 20th century. The book moves between Finnish nature and human inner life: winter silence, spring’s return, the sea’s swell and foam, love’s tests, social irony, and modern restlessness, all rendered in vivid, musical language.

L'estudiant de la Garrotxa by Josep Berga i Boix is a novel written in the late 19th century. Set between Girona and the stark valleys and cliffs of La Garrotxa, it follows a poor seminarian who discovers a talent for decorative painting, rises to local renown, and is pulled between priesthood, art, and his growing love for Margarida, the rector’s niece.

The Cat Who Went to Heaven is a 1930 novel by Elizabeth Coatsworth that won the Newbery Medal for excellence in American children's literature in 1931. On January 1, 2026, the novel entered the public domain in the USA.

Las Siete Partidas, o simplemente Partidas, son un cuerpo normativo redactado en Castilla durante el reinado de Alfonso X (1221-1284) con el objetivo de conseguir una cierta uniformidad jurídica del reino. Su nombre original era «Libro de las Leyes», y hacia el siglo XIV d.

Naamioita III-IV by Eino Leino is a collection of plays written in the early 20th century. It combines moral-psychological tableaux with historical tragedy, moving from medieval remorse to classical intrigue.

La figlia d'un ghibellino, vol. 1/2 by Giovanni Campiglio is a historical novel written in the early 19th century. Set around Milan at the dawn of the 15th century, it blends Guelph–Ghibelline strife with personal drama and adventure, centering on the young noble Arrigo Bianchi and a feared outlaw called the Guerrier Nero amid castles, bandit strongholds, and political upheaval.

La figlia d'un ghibellino, vol. 2/2 by Giovanni Campiglio is a historical novel written in the early 19th century. Set around Milan at the dawn of the fifteenth century, it entwines factional strife and siege warfare with a love tried by honor, centering on Arrigo Bianchi, the Pusterla family—especially Beatrice—and warlords such as Facino Cane and the rising captain Carmagnola.

Sébastien Roch by Octave Mirbeau is a novel written in the early 20th century. It follows a gentle provincial boy whose vain, status-seeking father sends him to a prestigious Jesuit college in Brittany, opening a critique of class pretension, clerical authority, and the fragility of innocence.

Complices by Robert de Traz is a collection of short stories written in the early 20th century. Through intimate first-person voices, it probes moral complicity, family loyalties, and the allure of transgression as perceived by children and adolescents.
